questions.q: In Anthropic's Messages API, where does the system prompt go?
options: A separate top-level system field, outside the messages array
Inside messages as a role called system
Inside messages as a role called developer
It is set once when the API key is created
questions.explain: Anthropic's messages array only ever contains user and assistant entries; system is its own top-level request field.

questions.q: Which two roles actually appear inside Anthropic's messages array?
options: system and user
user and assistant
human and bot
request and response
questions.explain: system lives outside the array; only user and assistant turns appear inside it.

questions.q: What does Anthropic's API do if you send two consecutive user messages by mistake?
options: It throws a validation error immediately
It silently drops the second message
It merges them into a single turn rather than erroring
It automatically inserts an assistant reply between them
questions.explain: Anthropic's documentation is explicit that consecutive same-role turns are combined into a single turn, not rejected as an error.

questions.q: How does OpenAI's Chat Completions API represent the system prompt?
options: As part of the model name string
As a separate top-level field, identical to Anthropic
OpenAI has no equivalent concept
As a message with role "system" inside the messages array
questions.explain: OpenAI puts system directly inside messages, alongside user and assistant, rather than using a separate top-level field.

questions.q: In the Messages API, how is conversation history maintained across turns?
options: Anthropic stores the conversation server-side under a session ID
The client resends the full messages array on every call; there is no server-side session
Only the latest message needs to be sent each time
History is stored automatically in the system field
questions.explain: There's no session concept in the Messages API — your application owns and resends the full conversation history on every request.
